The marker vocabulary is masked and clear. No source names this path, these parameters or these field names: they are Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-P4-020-1; ASM-B2-P4-020-1).
why: The legacy story's five operations belong to the dictionary owner in the target (RWB-P1-E1064-CON), and the module's endpoint inventory (TSD P4 T-A.1) has no dictionary read, so this slice cannot copy a path. It cannot borrow GET /admin/roles either, because that operation is the role catalogue of RWB-P4-E1016-APP and a second declaration of it would publish two shapes for one path. Root AGENTS.md rule 8 forbids inventing a value and requires the placeholder and a row, so the read is fixed here, its shape is published with the contract and the missing source is recorded rather than a path borrowed.

text: The approver of a dictionary governance load is a role that the matrix in force gives the Reference data A letter, and the SIT matrix fixture PM-2026.11 gives that letter to the reference data administrator row, which is the role that prepares and submits the load, so the approver in a test is a second person holding the same role. TSD P4 T6.1 gives no role an A in Reference data, so no role code is stated as a business value: the gate reads the letter from permission at the version in force and refuses every approval where the caller has none.
why: API-P4-006 declares the A right and FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-03 applies the four-eyes rule, but the RBAC matrix of TSD P4 T6.1 stops at C, R, U and D in the Reference data column. Under R-PREC the TSD outranks the story master, so a role code taken from the legacy story would contradict a higher source, and a role code invented here would break AGENTS.md rule 8. The letter and the rule are therefore kept exactly as the two documents state them and the identity is left to a matrix row, which is a data change and not a build.

text: A field whose is_personal is true needs at least one masking_rule row at the masking version in force, and a personal field with no row is masked for every role and reported as a coverage failure of the load; the count of personal fields among the 1,366 is not stated by any source, so the register reports the count it finds and no criterion asserts a fixed number.
why: FSD P4 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05 give the default (a personal field with no rule is masked) and TSD P4 T3.1 keys the policy on role_code, field_id and masking_version, but neither states how many fields are personal or how many rows a complete pack holds. A count invented here would be a business value, and a criterion on it would fail for a reason nobody can check.

text: After its checks pass, the gate calls the load owner once, POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve with the same Idempotency-Key, and the owner moves the version LOADED to APPROVED and to IN_FORCE from its valid-from date; the dictionary owner applies the rows through its reference-table handler for table code sys_fields; rwb-access writes no row, no version and no state.
why: The legacy story applies the load through DataDictionaryLoader.apply inside P1 and approves it through the monolith reference-load endpoint; in the target the submit and approve are the rwb-case reference-data contract's (DP-07) and the apply is P1's handler (RWB-P1-E1064-CON section 12.5), and the two are not described together anywhere. Choosing the owner's approve keeps one writer and one approver and lets the gate stay read-only, which is what DP-01 and DP-15 require of a service that owns none of the dictionary's tables.
